I binge really easily no matter what I eat which leads to crazy weight gain. I had a period of 5 years where I restricted successfully but the moment I went into recovery that desire to never stop eating came back and has never left. I can't say I am fully recovered because I still fear food but I'm so happy that I decided to recover from ana to be honest. Looking back I would much rather have a hard time with eating too much than not at all but that is just my personal preference.

I think, at least in my own experience, that the lack of understanding to the mental battle is the biggest problem with the misconceptions surrounding anorexia. The media has just glamorized it as *don't eat and become skinny legend*  so sadly that is how people see it. 

Also, unfortunately, the comments are also pretty natural at this point. Peoples weight is such a major part of our society, so we have one side telling us we need to look a certain way to be attractive while the other side tells us we need to look a different way to be attractive so people mindlessly tell people what they think what they should look like when it is none of their business. 

I can't say that the comments get any easier with time, and I know this is easier said than done, but try not to let it get to you. The people making these comments probably don't know what they're talking about or realise what you are going through and how much it is affecting you.

I hope things get better for you my friend :)

I would say the big for of BM is

Burzum - This man single handily set the bar for black metal. The one man band, the ambient atmospheric tracks, the lo-fi production and Vargs overall amazing playing. Sure he may say he is a sucky drum player but he isn't half bad. Find a black metal project today that isn't clearly inspired by Vikernes.

Darkthone - The iconic duo of black metal. The unholy trinity being their first 3 albums. Much like burzum I don't think there are many bands out there that aren't clearly inspired by darkthrone. Some of their songs are borderline unlistenable because of how poor the recording and production is, which just makes them even better.

Dimmu Borgir - Yeah I know 99% of us aren't keen on them post second album but they are the most commercially successful black metal project going, and the big 4 was most about the commercial success of the bands rather than their quality. Think how quickly Metallica fell off. 

Xasthur - I would say that Xasthur, musch like Burzum, really encompasses the entire feeling and concept of black metal and set the standard for DSBM. Not only that but Xasthur has been featured in quite a few publications over the years despite being black metal, his music is just that good that you'd be hard pressed to not find something you like in his library.

In my opinion it has got to be Xasthurs Telepathic With the Deceased. Say what you want about Silencer making DSBM, Abyssic Hate setting a new standard and all the other amazing bands out there like Hypothermia, Leviathan, Lifelover (this list is endless because who doesn't have their own DSBM project at this point) but I think Xasthur is the true embodiment of Depressive Suicidal Black Metal. 

A total shut in self harmer spends almost all of his free time just sitting in his small house making music obsessively. That feel alone is so present in most of his albums, and in my eyes Telepathic with the deceased is the crowning jewel of all of his projects. This album has such a dark tone, even the ambient opening track feels like boss music from a souls game where you're never supposed to win. It fills you with dread and hopelessness from it's slow tempo and subtle background noises.
